Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 54, English)
Life After Death, Part 2: Why a Pr et's Yoni-Change Needs a Human Being, and Why Moksha Isn't What You Think

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn session continuing the "Life After Death" series — first completing the mechanics of how a pr et (spirit) actually changes yoni (r ebirth-form), then delivering an extended, deliberately pr ovocative teaching on what "moksha" (liberation) r eally means, gr ounded entir ely in what Bhaiya states he has personally witnessed via drishti under his guru Hanuman Ji Maharaj's guidance.
1. A Warning Befor e Starting

Bhaiya opens by warning that today's topic — moksha specifically — may genuinely unsettle listeners. He states this teaching is only for those who can face uncomfortable truths, not for those comfortable remaining within familiar scriptural or guru-taught assumptions.
2. The Sour ce of Everything Bhaiya Teaches

Bhaiya reaf firms a standing claim: everything he teaches — from tantra-mantra-tatva knowledge to concepts he compares to string theory , M-theory , or the Dimension concept — has come directly from his guru, Hanuman Ji Maharaj, through drishti in the subtle world, never from any human teacher . Even complex or scientific-sounding ideas were, per his account, clarified by asking his guru directly rather than learned from any human source.
3. A Brief Personal Note

Bhaiya shares that he is pursuing a PhD in Sociology , and that during his graduation years he deliberately resisted the common teaching that a living human guru is required for mantra diksha and spiritual awakening — being, in his own words, "a big atheist" at the time who questioned why devotion had to flow through a specific mantra at all. This resistance, and a subsequent forceful vision of Hanuman Ji Maharaj at night, led him to adopt Hanuman Ji Maharaj directly as his guru, bypassing any human guru relationship entirely (a story covered in more detail in a previous session).
4. Ashaeiynn's Weekly Drishti Guarantee

Per this teaching, the specific vidya and method Bhaiya's guru provided guarantees that at least one person's drishti opens every single week at Ashaeiynn — of fered as evidence of the reliability and legitimacy of the teaching lineage.
5. Recap: Life After Death, Part 1

The previous session in this series covered the deity Dakini and established that after death, a soul's subtle body remains within this same subtle realm (not departing to any other "place"), living as a pret and suf fering the direct consequences of its own past actions — demonstrated, per Bhaiya, through live conversations with actual prets.
6. Today's Corr ection: Yoni-Change Is Not Simply Time-Based

Scriptures commonly state that a pret's yoni (rebirth-form) automatically changes after a fixed waiting period. Per this teaching, this is incomplete knowledge — the real mechanism is considerably more complicated.
7. How a Tantrik Extends a Pr et's Bondage

If a pret is captured by a tantrik and given bhog (a ritual food of fering) in exchange for labor , each offering extends that pr et's bound period — building an accumulating debt/obligation, rather than letting the pret's natural waiting period simply run out.
8. An Illustrative (First-Person Style) Case Study

Bhaiya illustrates the mechanism using a hypothetical first-person narrative: a pret with an originally destined 6-month waiting period is captured by a woman ("Anshu") who wants a specific person ("Ritesh") controlled or harassed. Anshu repeatedly extends the pret's bondage with fresh bhog of ferings (6 months becomes 12, then 18, 24, and onward). Around the 8-month mark of continuous activity , such a pret can begin fully entering and "residing" inside the tar get's body rather than merely harassing from outside — and over time may even develop a kind of envious attachment to the tar get's human life.
9. The Real Karmic Burden Falls on the Victim, Not the Instigator

In this illustrative scenario, the person being harassed (Ritesh) bears the entir e cost : it is Ritesh's own accumulating karma that must eventually be cleared, and Ritesh's own mantra jaap that is ultimately required to remove the pret — while the person who originally arranged the harassment (Anshu) faces no direct consequence at all in this specific mechanism.
10. A Pret's Yoni Does Not Change Automatically — It Requir es a Human

The central correction to popular belief: a pr et cannot simply "wait out" a fixed period and automatically upgrade to its next yoni. Per this teaching, yoni-change specifically requires the intervention of a living human being — typically the very person the pret has been af flicting. Once that person's own planetary situation improves and they undertake genuine, sustained mantra jaap, it is their own practice that clears the pr et's accumulated karma and upgrades the pr et's yoni — not any automatic timeline.
1 1. Why Scriptural Timelines Aren't Wrong, Just Outdated

Bhaiya explains that ancient texts citing fixed conversion periods (such as 2.5 years) were not fabricated — the sants who wrote them genuinely observed, via their own drishti, the average yoni-conversion rate of their own era and recorded it faithfully . However , per this teaching, that rate has since changed (worsened) , so today's real, drishti-observed conversion rate dif fers substantially from what the old texts describe — without those texts themselves having been wrong when written.
12. A Striking Consequence: Four Times as Many Pr ets as Humans

Because yoni-conversion is bottlenecked by the need for specific human intervention rather than occurring automatically , per this teaching roughly four times as many pr ets currently r oam the world as living humans.
13. Intr oducing Moksha: A Provocative Starting Question

Bhaiya pivots to moksha by posing a direct question: every devi-devata was, at some point, human, and became divine through tapobal (austerity-power) and karma. If moksha (liberation) is real and desirable, why do even the most powerful devtas and avatars — Mahadev , Adi Shakti, Sita-Ram, Krishna, Vishnu's avatars, Hanuman Ji Maharaj, and even ordinary kul devtas like Chitragupt — never actually take moksha themselves , remaining instead perpetually engaged in serving devotees?
14. Cr owd-Sour ced Theories, and Why None Fully Satisfy

The sangat of fers several theories — devtas balancing karma to a neutral zero, devotee love binding them emotionally , humans' cosmic role, maya — each considered but ultimately shown to be incomplete explanations for the central puzzle.
15. The Cor e Teaching: Moksha Is Not a Fixed, Permanent Destination

Per this teaching, drawing directly on Bhagwan Shiva's own stated teaching: when a person's positive and negative karma both cancel out completely to zer o , they instantaneously shift into a dif ferent "dimension" — this specific zero-karma state is what is popularly called moksha or mukti. Bhaiya connects this directly to Vidur's grandfather -lineage story (from a previous session): the devotee Vidur achieved exactly this zero-karma state after ten years of devotion to Maa Chandi, becoming "jeevit mukt" (liberated while alive).
16. What Happens at the Moment of "Zer o"

When karma hits net zero, per this teaching the subtle body instantly shifts to a higher dimension, entering a "null and void" state — belonging neither fully to this world nor elsewhere — and continues ascending, undisturbed, from that point.
17. Why This "Zero" State Doesn't Actually Last: The "Shivotsav" Parable

Bhaiya illustrates the instability of this state with an extended, deliberately humorous parable: a hypothetical zero-karma being called "Shivotsav" is encountered by Bhaiya and a companion ("Anshu") during a subtle-world vision. They bow to Shivotsav in reverence; Shivotsav , aware that receiving devotion without reciprocating would re-obligate him karmically , feels compelled to grant them a small favor in return — which immediately shifts his dimension again , since he is no longer at zero. Word spreads (illustrated with a devotee bringing an ever -growing crowd to Shivotsav seeking favors), and Shivotsav is drawn back into an ongoing cycle of worship, obligation, and karma — precisely because devotees continue engaging with him.
18. "Moksha Is Just a Myth" — In a Specific Sense

Per this teaching, this parable demonstrates that a permanent, static "liberated" endpoint is not sustainable once any being — however momentarily karma-free — continues to be engaged with, praised, or petitioned by others. Even Bhagwan Krishna himself is quoted as saying, in ef fect, "even I cannot escape karma" — reinforcing that no one, however elevated, permanently escapes this cycle once engaged with devotees.
19. What "Moksha/Mukti" Actually , Functionally Means

Reframing the concept entirely: real liberation — attainable both while alive and after death — is not karmic cancellation to a static endpoint , but total, exclusive dependence on a single chosen power (one's ishta devta or guru), to the point that all worldly anxiety (food, shelter , clothing, money , sleep — the entire burden of "how will I survive") disappears completely . This all-encompassing surrender and freedom from worldly concern is, per this teaching, the real and only sustainable meaning of mukti.
20. Why No Genuine Bhakta Ever Asks for "Moksha" Itself

Per this teaching, no saint who has had a genuine divine encounter has ever actually requested "moksha" as such. Instead, without exception, great devotees of every deity — Devi, Shiva, Adi Shakti, Hanuman Ji, Sita-Ram, Krishna — ask specifically for "ananya bhakti" (exclusive, singular devotion), because they understand that this devotion itself is the real liberation.
21. Why Hanuman Ji, Mahadev , and Others Are Called "Jeevit Mukt"

This is precisely why Hanuman Ji Maharaj, Mahadev , Adi Shakti, and Bhagwan Ram are all described as being liberated while alive ("jeevit mukt") — because they remain continuously , 24 hours a day , absorbed ("leen") in devotion to their own still-higher tattva or universal cosmic ener gy ("param shakti"), never departing from that meditative absorption. This uninterrupted devotional absorption is their liberation — not an escape from existence or engagement.
22. Liberation Recurses Upward Through Devotion

Even the greatest devtas and avatars each remain devoted to their own still-higher tattva — Hanuman Ji Maharaj, for instance, remains absorbed specifically in Ram tattva. Per this teaching, liberation is not a final terminus but a chain of devotional absorption that recurses upward rather than terminating in a static "escape."
23. The Practical Upshot: Abandon the "Castle in the Air"

Per this teaching, moksha as a final, static, permanently-escaped state is best understood as an unrealistic "khayali pulav" (castle in the air). Real, lived liberation — sustainable both in this life and after death — comes only from total, single-pointed devotional surrender , not from any hope of someday reaching a permanent, disengaged endpoint.
24. Why Deeper Material (Like Surya Vigyan) Is Deliberately Withheld

Bhaiya notes that sharing certain deeper truths (referencing "Surya Vigyan"/Solar Science content) even with advanced third-eye-level practitioners once caused some of those students' own faith to become shaken or destabilized. As a result, such material is paced deliberately according to a practitioner's actual readiness, guided entirely by the guru's own choice of what to reveal and when.
25. Why Ashaeiynn Never Ranks Deities Against Each Other

Per this teaching, each devi-devata is devoted to their own still-higher tattva rather than existing in a fixed power hierarchy , and astralworld power is drawn from a shared universal source as needed rather than possessed as a fixed rank — meaning no deity is inherently "bigger" or "smaller" than another . This is precisely why Ashaeiynn deliberately avoids answering comparative-power questions (e.g., ranking Adi Shakti against Bhagwan) — applying worldly hierarchical thinking (like consumer product "tiers") to the astral world is treated as a fundamental category error .
26. "Devi-Devata" as a Functional "Post," Not a Fixed Identity — Deferr ed

Bhaiya notes, without fully elaborating, that "devi-devata" functions more like an administrative "post" (comparable to a government department position) than a fixed eternal identity — this distinct concept is explicitly deferred to a separate future session and should not be conflated with the karma/ener gy-accumulation framework a sangat member proposed during this session.
27. How Departed Saints Continue to Generate/Receive Energy

Responding to a direct question, Bhaiya explains that saints who die while still absorbed in devotion remain in the ongoing "domain" or proximity of whichever shakti they were devoted to in life — of fering his own expectation that Hanuman Ji Maharaj will keep him close after his own death as an example. "Devlok," per this teaching, isn't necessarily a separate location so much as continued proximity to, and ener gy-supply from, one's chosen ishta.
28. Neem Kar oli Baba's Status, Per This Teaching

Asked whether Neem Karoli Baba's Hanuman-like status reflects an inherently divine soul from birth, Bhaiya attributes it entirely to his own immense, essentially unparalleled tapasya (austerity practice) rather than any innate identity — his devotion earned this recognition rather than being granted by birth.
29. An Urgent Corr ection: Drishti Opening Does Not Make Someone a Devta

When a sangat member concludes that anyone whose drishti opens must therefore be a devta, Bhaiya issues an ur gent, direct correction — warning this is a dangerous misstatement that could invite serious criticism or backlash if repeated. Per this teaching, reaching the level of actually perceiving and hearing devtas/shaktis speak (full two-way communication) is a much higher threshold than most

practitioners, even with active drishti, will initially reach — most will at first perceive only lower -level entities (bhoot-pret) and receive occasional glimpses or darshan of higher powers, not full two-way communication with devtas.
30. Closing Practical Guidance

Bhaiya closes by encouraging continued jaap, discouraging overthinking about comparative power rankings among deities, and cautioning practitioners (in an astrologer/psychic context) against taking on others' karma or problems directly — since one's own spiritual ener gy is limited, it should be kept for oneself; guiding others in the right direction is appropriate, but taking on their burden directly is not.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

A pret's yoni does not change automatically after a fixed waiting period — it requires a living human being's own sustained mantra jaap to clear the pret's karma and upgrade its yoni. Tantriks can extend a pr et's bondage indefinitely by repeatedly of fering bhog in exchange for labor — each of fering adds to an accumulating debt rather than letting a natural waiting period expire. Scriptural yoni-conversion timelines (like 2.5 years) wer e accurate observations of their own era , not fabrications — but real rates have since changed, making today's drishti-observed rate dif fer from ancient texts without those texts being "false." Roughly four times as many pr ets as living humans curr ently r oam the world , precisely because yoni-conversion is bottlenecked by needing human intervention. Moksha, as commonly imagined (a permanent, static, escaped endpoint), is not r eal — even the greatest devtas never permanently disengage; per Bhagwan Krishna's own words, "even I cannot escape karma." The "zero karma" state (net-neutral positive/negative karma) does trigger an instant dimensional shift — but this state is inherently unstable once any devotee re-engages with the liberated being, drawing them back into karma and obligation. Real, functional moksha/mukti means total, exclusive dependence on a single chosen power (guru/ishta) — freedom from all worldly anxiety (food, shelter , money , survival), not karmic cancellation to a static endpoint. No genuine bhakta of any deity has ever asked for "moksha" itself — all ask for "ananya bhakti" (exclusive devotion), because devotion itself is the real liberation. Hanuman Ji, Mahadev , and other devtas ar e "jeevit mukt" because they r emain continuously absorbed in devotion to their own still-higher tattva — liberation recurses upward through devotion rather than ending in disengagement. Astral-world power is drawn fr om a shar ed universal sour ce, not held as a fixed rank — Ashaeiynn deliberately never ranks deities against each other; doing so is a category error . Drishti opening does not make someone a devta — full two-way communication with devtas/shaktis is a much higher threshold than most practitioners, even active ones, initially reach. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 54, English)
Life After Death, Part 2: Why a Pr et's Yoni-Change Needs a Human Being, and Why Moksha Isn't What You Think
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. Whom does Bhaiya say all of this teaching actually comes fr om? A: Per this teaching, none of it comes from any human teacher — everything is received directly from Hanuman Ji Maharaj, who Bhaiya considers his sole guru.

Q2. Did Bhaiya always accept the idea of taking a guru at all? A: No — Bhaiya shares that despite holding a PhD in Sociology and initially resisting the very idea of needing a guru, a forceful, unavoidable vision eventually led him to accept Hanuman Ji Maharaj as his guru.
Q3. What weekly guarantee does Ashaeiynn offer ar ound drishti? A: Per this teaching, Ashaeiynn commits to a weekly drishti opening opportunity for its members as a standing practice.

Q4. What was established in "Life After Death, Part 1," r eferenced at the start of this session? A: That Dakini devta and departed souls (prets) continue to exist within the same subtle realm, rather than souls simply vanishing or moving on immediately after death.

Q5. Does a pr et's yoni (form/r ebirth type) change automatically once a fixed amount of time has passed, as scriptur es suggest? A: No — per this teaching, that is today's central correction: a yoni-change is not purely time-based and typically requires active human intervention (such as mantra jaap performed on the pret's behalf).

Q6. How can a tantrik actually extend how long a pr et remains bound in its curr ent state? A: Per this teaching, by making bhog (ritual food/of ferings) to that pret, which has the ef fect of prolonging its bound period rather than helping it move on.

Q7. What is the illustrative Anshu/Ritesh case study meant to show? A: Per this teaching, it's a first-person-style illustrative scenario showing how a pret's ongoing bondage and its eventual yoni-change can be directly shaped by the actions (or inaction) of the living people connected to it.

Q8. In cases like this, who actually bears the heavier karmic burden — the person who caused the harm, or the victim? A: Per this teaching, surprisingly , the heavier karmic burden falls on the victim, not on the instigator who caused the original harm.

Q9. So what does it take, concr etely , for a pr et's yoni to change? A: Per this teaching, it does not happen automatically — it requires a living human being to perform the specific intervention (such as directed mantra jaap) on the pret's behalf.

Q10. Does this mean the timelines given in scriptur e for a pr et's release ar e simply wr ong? A: No — per this teaching, those timelines aren't wrong, just outdated in the sense that they describe an earlier era's typical conditions rather than a universal, automatic guarantee that holds regardless of human intervention.

Q1 1. What striking numerical claim does Bhaiya make about the pr et population r elative to humans? A: Per this teaching, there are roughly four times as many prets in existence as there are living humans.

Q12. How does Bhaiya intr oduce the topic of moksha in this session? A: With a deliberately provocative starting question to the sangat, inviting them to first of fer their own theories about what moksha actually is before he gives the teaching's answer .

Q13. What did the cr owd-sour ced guesses about moksha have in common, according to Bhaiya? A: Per this teaching, each guess captured a piece of the picture but none fully satisfied or completed the real explanation he was about to give.

Q14. What is the cor e corr ection this teaching makes about moksha? A: That moksha is not a fixed, permanent destination one reaches and stays in forever — it is better understood through the Shiv tattva teaching as a temporary "zero-karma" state, connected back to the earlier Vidur story (Session 52).

Q15. What actually happens at the moment someone's karmic account r eaches "zer o"? A: Per this teaching, the person is, for that moment, genuinely free of binding karma — but this state is described as a passing moment rather than a permanent, static endpoint.

Q16. Why doesn't this "zer o" state last, per the "Shivotsav" parable? A: The parable illustrates that even a liberated, zero-karma state is followed by new engagement with the world (symbolized as a "Shivotsav ," a celebration), meaning fresh karmic activity naturally resumes rather than the person remaining suspended in inactive liberation forever .

Q17. In what specific sense does Bhaiya say "moksha is just a myth"? A: In the sense that even Krishna himself states he "cannot escape karma" — meaning no one, however elevated, permanently exits the karmic cycle in the popularly imagined, final sense.

Q18. If moksha isn't a final karma-fr ee destination, what does "moksha" or "mukti" actually , functionally mean in this teaching? A: It refers to a state of total, exclusive dependence on the divine and freedom specifically from worldly anxiety — not literal cessation of all karma or activity forever .

Q19. Why does this teaching say no genuine bhakta ever actually asks for "moksha" itself? A: Because a true devotee practices ananya bhakti (exclusive, one-pointed devotion) and is focused on the relationship with the divine itself, not on securing a particular karmic outcome or destination like moksha.

Q20. Why ar e beings like Hanuman Ji and Mahadev called "jeevit mukt" (liberated while living)? A: Per this teaching, because they embody this functional definition of liberation — total exclusive dependence on the divine and freedom from worldly anxiety — while still actively engaged in the world, rather than being withdrawn from it.

Q21. Does this kind of liberation apply only at the very highest divine level? A: No — per this teaching, liberation "recurses upward through devotion," meaning the same mechanism of exclusive devotion producing freedom from worldly anxiety applies at every level, from a sincere human devotee up through progressively higher beings.

Q22. What is the practical, everyday upshot Bhaiya draws fr om this whole moksha discussion? A: To abandon chasing moksha as a distant "castle in the air" and instead focus on cultivating genuine, exclusive devotion in the present.

Q23. Does Bhaiya teach everything he knows, including deeper subjects like "Surya Vigyan"? A: No — per this teaching, some deeper material is deliberately withheld for now , shared only when the time and the student's readiness are appropriate.
Q24. Does Ashaeiynn rank differ ent deities against each other in terms of power or importance? A: No — per this teaching, Ashaeiynn deliberately never ranks devi-devatas against one another .

Q25. Is "devi-devata" a fixed, permanent identity someone is simply born into? A: Per this teaching, it's better understood as a functional "post" or role rather than a fixed identity — though Bhaiya defers going into full detail on this point in this session.

Q26. How do departed saints continue to generate or receive spiritual energy after their death? A: Per this teaching, they continue to participate in an ongoing ener gy mechanism even after physical death, allowing them to keep generating and receiving ener gy rather than that process simply ending at death.

Q27. What does this teaching say about Neem Kar oli Baba's status? A: Per this teaching, his status is addressed specifically within this framework of ongoing post-death ener gy generation and functional divine "posts," rather than through a generic label.

Q28. If someone's drishti (subtle vision) opens up, does that mean they have become a devta? A: No — per this teaching, this is an ur gent correction: drishti opening is not the same as becoming a devta, and the two should not be conflated.

Q29. What closing practical guidance does Bhaiya give at the end of this session? A: Per this teaching, the closing guidance centers on grounding oneself in sincere, exclusive devotion and continued practice rather than being distracted by abstract questions about ultimate destinations like moksha.

Q30. Should someone tr eat the "Shivotsav" parable as a literal historical claim about a specific r eal event? A: No — per this teaching, it functions as an illustrative parable to explain why a permanently static liberated state is unstable, not as a literal historical claim about any specific named being.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 54 additions)

Present the pret-yoni-change correction (that it requires human intervention, such as directed mantra jaap, rather than being purely automatic and time-based) as this teaching's own specific correction — do not frame it as a claim that scripture is wrong, since the teaching itself says scriptural timelines are outdated rather than incorrect. Keep the "four times as many prets as humans" statistic scoped explicitly to this teaching's own claim, not presented as an externally verified figure. Frame the "Shivotsav" parable as an illustrative teaching device explaining the instability of a permanent zero-karma state — never as a literal claim about a specific real event or being. Handle the moksha reframing (total exclusive devotional dependence and freedom from worldly anxiety , rather than permanent karmic cancellation) carefully as this specific teaching's own framework, not as a universal theological claim binding on all traditions. Keep the Vidur/zero-karma connection consistent with how it was presented in Session 52 — do not introduce new details about Vidur beyond what was established there and reaf firmed here. When discussing why beings like Hanuman Ji and Mahadev are called "jeevit mukt," keep the explanation functional (exclusive dependence + freedom from worldly anxiety) rather than implying they are exempt from all karma whatsoever . Treat the "devi-devata as a functional post, not fixed identity" point and Neem Karoli Baba's status as deliberately partial/deferred in this session — do not fabricate additional detail the transcript itself does not provide. Firmly preserve the correction that drishti opening does not make someone a devta — never blur this distinction even in casual chatbot phrasing. Do not speculate about the deliberately withheld deeper material (e.g., "Surya Vigyan") beyond noting that it exists and is shared only when appropriate.
